questions.stem: A train 300 m long passes a pole in 15 seconds. What is its speed in km/h?
questions.explanation:
Speed = Length / Time = 300 / 15 = 20 m/s
Convert: 20 × 18/5 = 72 km/h
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A train travels at 54 km/h. How many seconds does it take to pass a pole if the train is 150 m long?
questions.explanation:
Speed = 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s
Time = Length / Speed = 150 / 15 = 10 seconds
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A train 200 m long passes a platform 400 m long in 36 seconds. What is the speed of the train in km/h?
questions.explanation:
Speed = (Train length + Platform length) / Time
= (200 + 400) / 36 = 600 / 36 = 50/3 m/s
Convert: 50/3 × 18/5 = 60 km/h
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A train moving at 25 m/s passes a pole in 12 seconds. What is the length of the train?
questions.explanation: Length = Speed × Time = 25 × 12 = 300 m
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A train 250 m long takes 50 seconds to cross a station 750 m long. Find the speed of the train in km/h.
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Two trains of lengths 120 m and 80 m travel in the same direction at 60 km/h and 40 km/h. How long does the faster train take to completely pass the slower one?
questions.explanation:
Relative speed = 60 − 40 = 20 km/h = 20 × 5/18 = 50/9 m/s
Total length = 120 + 80 = 200 m
Time = 200 / (50/9) = 200 × 9/50 = 36 seconds
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A train crosses a bridge of 300 m in 30 seconds and a pole in 10 seconds. Find the speed of the train.
questions.explanation:
Let train length = L, speed = S
Pass pole: L = S × 10
Pass bridge: L + 300 = S × 30
Subtract: 300 = 20S → S = 15 m/s
L = 15 × 10 = 150 m
Speed = 15 × 18/5 = 54 km/h
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Two trains of lengths 100 m and 150 m run toward each other at 30 km/h and 45 km/h. In how many seconds do they completely pass each other?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Train A (120 m, 54 km/h) overtakes train B (80 m, 36 km/h) traveling in the same direction. How many seconds does A take to completely pass B?
questions.explanation:
Speed A = 54 × 5/18 = 15 m/s; Speed B = 36 × 5/18 = 10 m/s
Relative speed = 15 − 10 = 5 m/s
Total length = 120 + 80 = 200 m
Time = 200 / 5 = 40 seconds
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A train at 72 km/h takes 30 seconds to pass a cyclist moving in the same direction at 36 km/h. Find the length of the train.
questions.explanation:
Relative speed = 72 − 36 = 36 km/h = 36 × 5/18 = 10 m/s
Length = Relative speed × Time = 10 × 30 = 300 m
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A train passes a platform 300 m long in 40 s and a pole in 20 s. Find the length of the train.
questions.explanation:
Time for platform − time for pole = extra time for platform length
Extra time = 40 − 20 = 20 s covers 300 m
Speed = 300/20 = 15 m/s
Train length = 15 × 20 = 300 m
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Two trains of lengths 120 m and 130 m run toward each other at 60 km/h and 30 km/h. In how many seconds do they completely pass each other?
questions.explanation:
Relative speed = 60 + 30 = 90 km/h = 90 × 5/18 = 25 m/s
Total length = 120 + 130 = 250 m
Time = 250 / 25 = 10 seconds
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A train at 80 km/h crosses a bridge of 500 m in 36 seconds. Find the length of the train.
questions.explanation:
Speed = 80 × 5/18 = 200/9 m/s
Total distance = Speed × Time = 200/9 × 36 = 800 m
Train length = 800 − 500 = 300 m
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Train A (80 km/h) and train B (120 km/h) leave from P and Q (400 km apart) toward each other simultaneously. How far from P do they meet?
questions.explanation:
Relative speed = 80 + 120 = 200 km/h
Time to meet = 400/200 = 2 hours
Distance covered by A (from P) = 80 × 2 = 160 km
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Two trains of equal length cross each other in 12 seconds when running in opposite directions at 60 and 90 km/h. Find the length of each train.
questions.explanation:
Relative speed = 60 + 90 = 150 km/h = 150 × 5/18 = 125/3 m/s
Total distance = 125/3 × 12 = 500 m
Each train = 500/2 = 250 m
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A train at 72 km/h passes a man running at 36 km/h in the same direction in 10 seconds. Find the train's length.
questions.explanation:
Relative speed = 72 − 36 = 36 km/h = 36 × 5/18 = 10 m/s
Length = 10 × 10 = 100 m
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A train 320 m long runs at 80 km/h. How many seconds does it take to cross a bridge of 480 m?
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A train running at 4/5 of its usual speed reaches the destination 40 minutes late. Find its usual time for the journey.
questions.explanation:
Let usual time = t minutes
At 4/5 speed, time taken = t × 5/4
Extra time = 5t/4 − t = t/4 = 40 minutes
t = 160 minutes = 2 hours 40 minutes
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A train passes two persons walking in the same direction at 3 km/h and 6 km/h in 12 and 10 seconds respectively. Find the speed of the train.
questions.explanation:
Let speed = v km/h = v×5/18 m/s; length = L
Person 1: L = (v−3) × 5/18 × 12
Person 2: L = (v−6) × 5/18 × 10
12(v−3) = 10(v−6)
12v − 36 = 10v − 60
2v = −24 → this gives negative v.
Swap: Person 1 walks faster: 6 km/h in 12s, person 2 at 3 km/h in 10s
L = (v−6)×5/18×12 = (v−3)×5/18×10
12(v−6) = 10(v−3)
12v−72 = 10v−30
2v = 42 → v = 21 km/h
L = (21−3)×5/18×10 = 18×50/18 = 50 m
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Train A starts from P toward Q (300 km away) at 60 km/h. Train B starts from Q toward P 1 hour later at 90 km/h. How far from P do they meet?
questions.explanation:
In A's first hour: A covers 60 km. Remaining gap = 240 km
Let t = hours after B starts; A and B together close 240 km:
60t + 90t = 240 → t = 240/150 = 1.6 hours
Total time for A = 1 + 1.6 = 2.6 hours
Distance from P = 60 × 2.6 = 156 km
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Two trains of lengths 180 m and 120 m run toward each other at 30 m/s and 20 m/s. How many seconds do they take to completely cross each other?
questions.explanation:
Relative speed = 30 + 20 = 50 m/s
Total length = 180 + 120 = 300 m
Time = 300 / 50 = 6 seconds
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A train A (100 m) travels opposite to train B (200 m). They pass each other in 12 seconds. Train A runs at 20 m/s. Find the speed of train B.
questions.explanation:
Relative speed = Total length / Time = 300 / 12 = 25 m/s
Relative speed = Speed A + Speed B (opposite directions)
25 = 20 + Speed B
Speed B = 5 m/s
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A train passes a platform 200 m long in 20 seconds and a man standing on it in 12 seconds. Find the length and speed of the train.
questions.explanation:
Speed = Platform length / (Time difference) = 200 / (20 − 12) = 200/8 = 25 m/s
Train length = Speed × Time for man = 25 × 12 = 300 m
Verify: (300+200)/25=20s ✓ and 300/25=12s ✓
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: A train overtakes a man walking opposite to it at 5 km/h in 18 seconds and another man at 10 km/h (opposite direction) in 15 seconds. Find the train's length.
questions.explanation:
Let train speed = v km/h; length = L metres
Person 1 (opposite, 5 km/h, 18s): L = (v+5) × 5/18 × 18 = 5(v+5)
Person 2 (opposite, 10 km/h, 15s): L = (v+10) × 5/18 × 15 = 25(v+10)/6
5(v+5) = 25(v+10)/6
6(v+5) = 5(v+10)
6v + 30 = 5v + 50 → v = 20 km/h
L = 5 × (20+5) = 125 m
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude

questions.stem: Trains T1 (60 km/h) and T2 (90 km/h) start simultaneously from P and Q toward each other. After they cross, T1 takes 9 hours to reach Q. How many hours does T2 take to reach P after crossing?
questions.explanation:
After two trains cross, their remaining times satisfy: t₂ = t₁ × (V₁/V₂)²
t₂ = 9 × (60/90)² = 9 × (2/3)² = 9 × 4/9 = 4 hours

**Proof:** Let meeting point split PQ into 2k (T1's covered) and 3k (T2's covered) since V1:V2=2:3.
T1 remaining = 3k/60; T2 remaining = 2k/90 = k/45. Ratio = (3k/60)/(k/45) = 135/60 = 9/4.
t₂ = 9 ÷ (9/4) = 4 hours ✓
questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
